name: Factory
description: Spec work becomes merged code: a stage-1 spec child is approved by its merge, the agent, human and release seats deliver in their lanes, one exit rule decides who merges, and the epic records its state.

steps.instructions: Rework the spec, ADR and any amended contracts to answer the review findings; keep the approved direction intact. The kickoff applied the chosen labels to the epic before this move, so the mode is set before the spec PR exists. This spec's integration branch is the one it records (`integration: <epic>`), forked from `main` at the spec sha before the PR exists; this PR heads the spec child's key and targets that branch, never `main`. The reslice window is the spec PR unmerged, or merged with no child in a started status: a change inside it is an added commit on the same head, or one revision PR on the same spec child after the merge, with the whole revised set published before review and the existing children reconciled in place; then return to spec_review for a fresh PASS. A rework is additive; a rewrite follows shared `## Delivery`. No second spec PR is open at once. Publish the whole slice first with to-tickets: every child under the epic, in `backlog`, in stage order, each with its project and planned owner (the human lane's is the live `human` seat) and `Branch: <epic>` for delivery children, `Branch: main` for the release child; a single-ticket breakdown is one delivery child plus the final-stage release. Publish the final-stage release child last, in `backlog`. Then open one reviewable pull request at the exact head against the integration branch, carrying the proposed breakdown, linked to this ticket; the merge approves the set, so create no child after the merge that approves its set. The freeze latches once the spec has merged and any child is in a started status (anything but `backlog`, `todo`, `done`, `cancelled`): a real change is a new epic, the old epic runs to its release, and the affected acceptance is recorded as superseded and cited. The release readback runs in the Planner's acceptance after the release merge, and the cancelled sweep in the run that cancels the epic; no condition's only trigger is a ticket that closes. Move the ticket to spec_review: the linked spec PR is the handoff, the move is your last action. This ticket is the epic's stage-1 spec child: its merge approves the spec and the breakdown, so never close it yourself and never link the spec PR to the epic. An external blocker moves the ticket to blocked with the reason.

Review the spec pull request at its exact head against the ticket, the approved direction, the proposed breakdown and the repository standards. Do not rewrite the spec. The head is the spec child's key and the base is the integration branch; a rework adds a commit, and a rewrite follows shared `## Delivery`. The published set carries every child's planned owner. A second open spec pull request, a spec pull request linked to the epic, a prefixed head, or a reslice after the freeze is a FAIL: comment the findings, then move the ticket back to spec_progress. PASS: post the PASS at the exact head, leave the pull request open, then move the ticket to awaiting_merge. Review only an open pull request: if the link is not open, there is nothing to review, so comment the state and move the ticket back to spec_progress. The release readback and the cancelled sweep are the Planner's runs, never conditions on a closing ticket. Never merge or enable auto-merge on a spec pull request. Never review or merge your own work.

Implement this ticket as one reviewable pull request. Read the ticket, its spec and the repository conventions first; reproduce any demonstrated failure before fixing it. Run the check that covers the diff with a finite timeout. Link the PR to this ticket, then move it to in_review: the linked PR is the handoff, the move is your last action. Never merge and never review your own work. An external blocker moves the ticket to blocked with the reason. Planner-owned spec text belongs in spec_progress, not here.

Implement this ticket as one reviewable pull request; this column is the human's delivery. Read the ticket, its spec and the repository conventions first. Run the check that covers the diff with a finite timeout. Link the PR to this ticket, then move it to human_review: the linked PR is the handoff, the move is your last action. Never merge and never review your own work. An external blocker moves the ticket to blocked with the reason. A conflict that lands here is resolved inside the PR, then moved to the review column that owns the work. Planner-owned spec text belongs in spec_progress, not here.

Deliver the release ticket as one reviewable pull request: follow `roles/release.md`. Link the PR to this ticket, then move it to release_review: the linked PR is the handoff, the move is your last action. Never merge and never review your own work. An external blocker moves the ticket to blocked with the reason.

Review the linked pull request at its exact head against the ticket's acceptance criteria and the repository standards, using the method and the exit rule in `code-review`. The exit rule decides the merge or a move to awaiting_merge; a merge completes this ticket, so do not move it. On a blocking finding, comment the evidence and move the ticket back to in_progress. Review only an open pull request: if the link is not open, there is nothing to review, so comment the state and move the ticket back to in_progress. Never enable auto-merge. Never review or merge your own work.

Review the human's pull request at its exact head against the ticket's acceptance criteria and the repository standards, using the method and the exit rule in `code-review`. The exit rule decides the merge or a move to awaiting_merge; a merge completes this ticket, so do not move it. On a blocking finding, comment the evidence and move the ticket back to human_progress. Review only an open pull request: if the link is not open, there is nothing to review, so comment the state and move the ticket back to human_progress. Never enable auto-merge. Never review or merge your own work. A spec pull request is reviewed at spec_review, not here.

Review the release pull request at its exact head against the ticket's acceptance criteria and the repository standards, using the method and the exit rule in `code-review`. The exit rule decides the merge or a move to awaiting_merge; a merge completes this ticket, so do not move it. On a blocking finding, comment the evidence and move the ticket back to release_progress. Review only an open pull request: if the link is not open, there is nothing to review, so comment the state and move the ticket back to release_progress. Never enable auto-merge. Never review or merge your own work.

Merge the reviewed pull request at its exact head when you are satisfied; the merge completes this ticket, so do not move it. This column is for a spec approval or a review the exit rule sent here. A spec child's merge approves the spec, its proposed breakdown and the published children, and wakes the Planner to promote the frontier. If it should change first, move it to spec_progress for planner-owned spec text, in_progress for agent delivery, human_progress for human delivery, or release_progress for a release, with the reason. Delete the head branch when you merge. Never enable auto-merge: this column exists so the merge is an explicit human act, and an armed pull request would merge on its checks without one.

Triage why the ticket stopped. Planner-owned spec work moves to spec_progress; human work to human_progress; agent delivery to in_progress; a release to release_progress. `blocked` is triage only — a missing input or an external condition — and a dependency wait never comes here: it is a `--blocked-by` blocker the platform releases. A cancelled or deleted blocker is not a delivery, so the woken run records the finding here for the Planner. A triaged ticket returns to the lane its timeline records. Unblock or cancel; nothing else stays parked.
